name: diagnosing-bugs: upstream vs compact local candidate
hypothesis: Reducing mandatory diagnostic stages for already-localized deterministic defects may reduce input/output use without lowering independently graded task outcomes.

treatment.status: local experimental derivative; not an upstream release
treatment.change: Only SKILL.md body changed. Frontmatter, UI metadata, HITL helper and license preserved. No task-specific implementation advice.

bench.source: Independent historical defects, selected and checked in before this candidate revision.
bench.selection: All three existing lru-cache tasks, without post-result selection.

calibration.use: difficulty pilot only; never pooled into validation

validation.order: adjacent baseline/treatment pairs, baseline first, existing protocol

stopping: Do not edit either Skill, bench, runtime configuration or compiled harness during a phase. No retries, replacement samples, outcome-driven trial additions or aggregation with earlier studies. Errors/drift stop calls; retain partial records.
interpretation: Three related positive bug-fix tasks from one repository: indicative within-bench revision evidence, not general utility or installation benefit. No negative-trigger inference. Existing 9-facet warning retained.
costs: Report actual input/output usage, cached input from saved JSON events when available, and executor duration. No monetary/billing claim.
reproducibility: Preserve declaration, source inputs, compiled runner and source patch, call ledger, manifests, receipts, transcripts and delivered workspaces. Offline regrade reproduces observed scores; new model runs reproduce procedure, not identical samples.
